chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from al-Rabīʿ ibn Muḥammad al-Muslī, from Muḥammad ibn Marwān, who said:
I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) saying: “Indeed, the Imam hears in the belly of his mother.”

So when he is born, it is inscribed between his shoulders: “And the Word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice; there is none who can alter His Words, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.”
Then when the command comes to him, Allah makes for him a pillar of light by which he sees what the people of every town are doing.”

key_terms.الْإِمَامَ: the divinely appointed Imam being described in the narration
key_terms.بَطْنِ أُمِّهِ: his mother’s womb, indicating a state before birth
key_terms.صِدْقًا وَعَدْلًا: in truth and justice, describing the perfection of the divine word
key_terms.عَمُودًا مِنْ نُورٍ: a pillar of light granted by Allah as a means of perception
key_terms.كَلِمَةُ رَبِّكَ: the word of your Lord, expressing divine truth and decree
key_terms.يُبْصِرُ بِهِ: he sees by it, referring to divinely enabled vision or awareness

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the Imam’s knowledge and signs from birth?
ai.summary: This hadith describes distinctive signs and divinely granted perception associated with the Imam, beginning from before birth and continuing when the authority comes to him. It also incorporates a Qur’anic phrase to express the truthfulness and justice of the divine word, while presenting the Imam as aided by Allah through a light by which matters are perceived.
